# Weights and direction

## How the weight is computed

The rule was decided with Allard Mees on 4 November 2026. It keeps the equal share of the source paper
(Thiery, Mees, Tolle and Wigg-Wolf 2021, section 4) but no longer counts the question mark as one more
possibility: the question mark halves the weight. It is implemented in [`py/weights.py`](https://github.com/leiza-scit/samian-amt/blob/main/py/weights.py):

    amt_weight = (1 / n_possibilities) * (1/2 if a question mark, else 1)      (two decimals)

| Source string | n_possibilities | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| no AND, no OR | 1 | one entity |
| AND | 1 | all entities hold; each keeps the full weight |
| OR | number of entities | exactly one holds; the weight is shared |

`n_questionmark` is 1 if the string contains a question mark, else 0. "A or B?" therefore gives 0.25 to each
(under the former rule of the paper 0.33), "A or B or C?" gives 0.17, and "A and B?" still gives 0.5 to each. A
string that mixes AND and OR is not covered. Cases (checked by the self-test, `python py/weights.py`):

| String | Relation | Entities | ? | Possibilities | Weight | FW type | Expected on the relation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Rheinzabern` | `actor--productioncentre` | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1.0 | Certainty | yes |
| `Rheinzabern?` | `actor--productioncentre` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0.5 | Uncertainty | yes |
| `Kräherwald and Rheinzabern` | `actor--productioncentre` | 2 | 0 | 1 | 1.0 | Vagueness | yes |
| `Kräherwald and Rheinzabern?` | `actor--productioncentre` | 2 | 1 | 1 | 0.5 | FuzzinessWobbliness | yes |
| `Pfaffenhofen or Westerndorf` | `actor--productioncentre` | 2 | 0 | 2 | 0.5 | Vagueness | yes |
| `Pfaffenhofen or Westerndorf?` | `actor--productioncentre` | 2 | 1 | 2 | 0.25 | FuzzinessWobbliness | no |
| `Heiligenberg and Ittenwiller and Kräherwald and Rheinzabern and Waiblingen-Beinstein?` | `actor--productioncentre` | 5 | 1 | 1 | 0.5 | FuzzinessWobbliness | yes |
| `15/17 or 18 or 18/31` | `informationcarrier--potform` | 3 | 0 | 3 | 0.33 | Vagueness | yes |
| `24 or 27 or 33` | `informationcarrier--potform` | 3 | 0 | 3 | 0.33 | Vagueness | yes |
| `33 or 38?` | `informationcarrier--potform` | 2 | 1 | 2 | 0.25 | FuzzinessWobbliness | yes |
| `dish or bowl?` | `informationcarrier--potform` | 2 | 1 | 2 | 0.25 | FuzzinessWobbliness | yes |
| `32?` | `informationcarrier--potform` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0.5 | Uncertainty | yes |
| `18/31?` | `informationcarrier--potform` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0.5 | Uncertainty | yes |
| `Lezoux?` | `informationcarrier--productioncentre` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0.5 | Uncertainty | yes |
| `Kräherwald and Rheinzabern` | `informationcarrier--productioncentre` | 2 | 0 | 1 | 1.0 | Vagueness | no |
| `Lezoux or Vichy ?` | `actor--productioncentre` | 2 | 1 | 2 | 0.25 | FuzzinessWobbliness | no |
| `South Gaul?` | `informationcarrier--productioncentre` | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0.5 | Uncertainty | yes |
| `A or B or C?` | `informationcarrier--potform` | 3 | 1 | 3 | 0.17 | FuzzinessWobbliness | yes |

The former rule (`1 / (n_questionmark + n_possibilities)`) and the exports agreed on every one of the 95,819
existing centre edges; the exported weights of strings with OR and question mark differ from the new rule,
which Allard Mees re-derives from the strings (the weights in the database export are ignored).

## Frequency shares (additional information, not a weight)

For an OR of forms the database knows how often each form occurs. [`py/frequency.py`](https://github.com/leiza-scit/samian-amt/blob/main/py/frequency.py)
divides the number of vessels of each alternative by the number of vessels of all alternatives (level A, the
whole database): "31 or 31R" gives 9,070 / 11,302 = 0.8025 and 2,232 / 11,302 = 0.1975. The method is called
*probability based on frequency share* (local name `sam:FrequencyShare`, not yet in
the FW ontology). The shares are a hint for the archaeologist to check an existing uncertainty against the
distribution in the database. They are not written to `fw:hasDegreeOfConnection`, do not enter the chains,
and a question mark does not change them. In `dist/chains.ttl` they stand beside the hextuple as
`sam:frequencyShare`, `sam:frequencyCount`, `sam:frequencyTotal`, `sam:frequencyLevel` and
`sam:frequencyMethod`. Planned: the potter's own repertoire (smoothed, with count and status) and the stamp
(PRIMER.md, step S4a).

## From quadruple to hextuple

An AMT statement is a reified quadruple: `rdf:subject`, `rdf:predicate`, `rdf:object`, `amt:weight`. The
[FW ontology](https://github.com/caa-datadragons/FW_Ontology) (`http://w3id.org/fw_ontology/`, prefix `fw:`)
adds two elements, which make it a hextuple, and an optional link to the source:

| Element | Carries | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `fw:hasDegreeOfConnection` | the weight; the same as `amt:weight` (the AMT engine reads both) | `0.33` |
| `fw:hasType` | the kind of fuzziness | an individual of `fw:FW_Type`: `fw:Certainty`, `fw:Uncertainty`, `fw:Vagueness` or `fw:FuzzinessWobbliness`; `fw:Certainty` is written for a certain statement and is never assumed (a statement without type is read as `fw:Vagueness`) |
| `fw:hasMethod` | how the weight was obtained | `fw:EqualShareRule`, the rule above; `fw:implementedBy` is meant to point to [`py/weights.py`](https://github.com/leiza-scit/samian-amt/blob/main/py/weights.py) ([triple](https://github.com/leiza-scit/samian-amt/blob/main/ontology/fw-implemented-by.ttl)) |
| `fw:derivedFrom` | what the weight rests on (optional) | a `fw:TextEvidence` node with the source string (`fw:sourceString`); all statements of one string share the node |

The type follows from the pattern of the string:

| Pattern | Source | FW type |
|---|---|---|
| `certain` | one entity, no question mark, no AND, no OR (weight 1.0) | `fw:Certainty` |
| `q` | question mark only | `fw:Uncertainty` |
| `or` | OR, no question mark | `fw:Vagueness` |
| `and` | AND, no question mark | `fw:Vagueness` |
| `q+or`, `q+and` | question mark with OR or AND | `fw:FuzzinessWobbliness` |

Which patterns are expected depends on the relation (the others are flagged, not rejected):

| Relation | Expected patterns |
|---|---|
| `actor--productioncentre` | `and`, `or`, `q`, `q+and` |
| `informationcarrier--potform` | `or`, `q`, `q+or` |
| `informationcarrier--productioncentre` | `q` |

The source string is kept exactly in the evidence node, and the step `chains` reads `dist/chains.ttl` back
and checks that every statement leads to its string, with the weight, type and method the rule gives. As a
counter-check, weight, type and the number of edges alone rebuild the string up to the order of the entities
and the spelling.

**Derived statements.** AMT.engine 0.6.0 and the reference reasoner of this repository agree on the type and
method of what the reasoner derives: a role chain gives the derived statement the logic as its method (for
example `amt:ProductLogic`) and the common type of its antecedents, or `fw:FuzzinessWobbliness` if they differ
(a statement without type counts as `fw:Vagueness`; `fw:Certainty` adds no fuzziness, so a chain of certain statements stays certain and a certain statement next to another type gives that type); an inverse takes the type of the statement it comes from
and has no method; of several paths to the same pair the one with the highest weight wins.

## Is the weight the same in both directions?

**Yes, for inverse roles the weight is the same in both directions.** If a carrier is of a potform
with degree 0.9, then the potform is the type of that carrier with degree 0.9. This is how AMT defines
an inverse, and it is also what the statement means.

## Why

1. **It is the rule of the AMT ontology.** The `amt:InverseRule` states: *"Add an edge (b -inverse-> a)
   with weight w."* The inverse edge copies the weight of its antecedent.
2. **It is the same statement.** An AMT edge is a statement about a pair with a degree of truth, read as
   a fuzzy relation. The inverse of a fuzzy relation is its transpose with the same membership degrees.
   `Carrier hasType Potform (0.9)` and `Potform isTypeOf Carrier (0.9)` are one statement read from two
   ends. If the two degrees differed, they would not be inverses but two different statements.
3. **The derived roles behave the same way.** All six fuzzy-logic operators of AMT (Goedel, Product,
   Lukasiewicz, Einstein, Geometric mean, Hamacher) are symmetric in their arguments. A chain read
   backwards uses the same weights, so `potformToCentre` and `centreToPotform` carry the same degree,
   and so do the other two pairs.

## What breaks the symmetry

The symmetry holds because the weight is a degree of truth. Other quantities look like weights
and are **not** all symmetric. Apart from the first row they should not be stored in `amt:weight`:

| Quantity | Example | Same in both directions? | Where it belongs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Degree of truth or certainty of the statement | the attribution of a carrier to a centre holds with 0.5 (recorded as uncertain) | yes | `amt:weight` |
| Conditional share | 40 % of the carriers of a potform are attributed to a centre, but only 10 % of that centre's carriers are of this potform | no | a separate measure on the pair |
| Normalised alternatives | a carrier has two possible centres, weights 0.5 and 0.5 so that they sum to 1 | no: the sum is taken per source node, so the inverse edges would sum differently | normalise when reading, or keep as a separate measure |
| Number of supporting carriers | twelve carriers support the association of a potform with a centre | yes, but it is a count, not a degree | a separate measure |

## Conventions for the model

1. **Assert one direction only.** Assert the roles in the direction of the source data (`hasType`,
   `hasProductionCentre`, `worksAt`) and let the inverse axioms create the other direction. If both
   directions are asserted with different weights, the data contradicts itself.
2. **Take the weight from the rule.** `py/weights.py` computes it from the source string. AND keeps the
   full weight for every entity (1.0, or 0.5 with a question mark); OR shares it (one over the number of
   alternatives, one more with a question mark). Nothing is normalised afterwards.
3. **Put shares and counts elsewhere.** If the question "how many carriers" or "what fraction" matters,
   compute it as its own measure on the pair, in the direction in which it is asked.
4. **Check the symmetry.** A consistency check (a SPARQL query on the reasoned graph) can report every
   pair of inverse edges whose weights differ. It should return nothing.
